analysis.title: Nvidia's 75% problem: the next China shock is coming
key_insights: US AI hardware and infrastructure names have sold off sharply while Chinese competitors have held up. TS Lombard argues the next AI disruption could be China becoming the world's low-cost supplier of compute, similar to solar and batteries.
China's semiconductor ETF (3191 HK) has outperformed the SOX over the past month, with most of the relative strength coming in the past few sessions.

Nvidia's share of Chinese data-center AI accelerator shipments fell to 34% in H1 2026, with Huawei at 28%. TS Lombard argues US export restrictions are accelerating China's domestic AI ecosystem and may create Nvidia's next major competitor.

China added roughly ten times as much generating capacity as the US in 2025. TS Lombard argues compute demand could migrate toward the cheapest power as US data-center expansion faces political resistance.
Inner Mongolia data-center hubs pay about 4.7 cents per kWh, roughly half the US industrial average. Electricity cost could become a key differentiator as compute commoditizes.

Open-weight models account for 72% of tokens on OpenRouter but 27% of spending. Chinese labs account for 69% of tokens. TS Lombard argues value shifts toward distribution and cheap compute as models become interchangeable.
With Nvidia gross margins around 75%, Chinese competitors have a large margin pool to attack. TS Lombard argues China needs to deliver sufficient compute at lower prices, not better chips.

Solar module prices have fallen 95% and battery pack prices 90% as Chinese manufacturers came to dominate. TS Lombard sees a similar dynamic in AI compute, with the risk to Western tech being structurally lower margins rather than weaker demand.
The Market Ear notes the SMHC ETF has existed only since June and has halved from its summer highs. It suggests expressing the thesis through low-delta upside options in SMHC.

market_movers.rationale: China share of data-center AI accelerator shipments fell to 34% in H1 2026 and Huawei is at 28%. Gross margins near 75% give Chinese competitors a large margin pool to attack.
China semiconductor ETF has shown relative strength despite the US AI selloff, though it has halved from its summer highs since its June launch. The Market Ear suggests low-delta upside options.

sector_views.rationale: Relative strength versus the SOX and a potential rotation, supported by domestic substitution, cheaper power and scale.
Risk of structurally lower margins if China becomes the low-cost compute supplier. Names have already sold off.

trade_ideas.description: Buy low-delta upside options (calls) in SMHC
trade_ideas.rationale: Chinese semis show relative strength despite the broader AI selloff, and TS Lombard's China low-cost compute thesis supports further upside.

risk_factors: Structurally lower margins for Western AI and tech companies if China becomes the low-cost compute supplier.
Further erosion of Nvidia's China market share to Huawei and other domestic suppliers.
SMHC has already halved from its summer highs and has a short trading history.
